references.text: The preceding verses describe the first three rows of gemstones on the breastpiece, which together with the fourth row make up the twelve stones representing the twelve tribes of Israel.
Parallel text describing the actual construction of the breastpiece with the fourth row of gemstones: chrysolite, onyx, and jasper.
Mentions onyx stones and other gemstones to be collected as offerings for the sanctuary, including stones for the breastpiece.
Ezekiel describes the king of Tyre's splendor with many of the same gemstones, including chrysolite (tarshish), onyx, and jasper.
Revelation describes the foundations of the new Jerusalem adorned with gemstones, including jasper and chrysolite, reflecting the stones of the breastpiece.
The first mention of the onyx stone (shoham) in the Bible, found in the land of Havilah.
The foundation of the heavenly city completes the symbolism from the priest's breastpiece, linking the tribes of Israel with the new creation.
